items.title: CM Afridi slams Governor Kundi for 'unconstitutional' meetings, claims move intended to provoke KP govt
items.description: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Wednesday slammed Governor Faisal Karim Kundi for holding “unconstitutional” meetings, contending that the move was an “attack on democracy”. His remarks came a day after Governor Kundi chaired a meeting with the KP chief secretary and inspector general (IG) on the province’s security situation. Addressing the 60th cabinet meeting in Peshawar, Afridi said that the KP governor, who belonged to the PPP, staged a “drama” yesterday by summoning the meeting and termed the move “unconstitutional”. “The governor convening such a meeting in the presence of a provincial government with a two-thirds majority is unacceptable,” he said. “The provincial assembly, cabinet and government are fully functional and intact,” the PTI leader asserted, terming Kundi’s act an “attack on the Constitution and democracy”. Afridi contended that the purpose of the governor’s “unconstitutional activities” was to “provoke the provincial government and force it to react”. However, he advised PTI workers to stay peaceful and abide by the law and the Constitution. Calling on the province’s chief secretary and IG, the chief minister urged them not to comply with any unconstitutional or illegal order from anyone if he does not order them to do so. He reiterated that KP’s people and administration had made “countless sacrifices” in the fight against terrorism. “If someone pushes you to follow any unconstitutional order, do not follow it. It can damage our province or the country.” He also called on the chief secretary to urge the provincial administration not to indulge in any unconstitutional activity and to take action against those who were accused of corrupt practices. The chief minister then took aim at Kundi’s PPP, blaming ex-president Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, along with General Yahya Khan, for the separation of East Pakistan, now Bangladesh. He accused President Asif Ali Zardari of “intending to make another East Pakistan here“. “We will not allow any conspiracy to break up Pakistan to succeed,” he asserted. “The party that raised the slogan of democracy separated Bangladesh from Pakistan in the past for its personal interests,” he alleged. “Prioritising personal interests over national interests has been the PPP’s practice,” he further claimed. Responding to Afridi, Kundi said on Geo News ’ programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath ’ said he called the meeting in light keeping in view the prevalent terrorism in the province. He then went on accusing the PTI of facilitating and supporting terrorism. The remarks by the CM and the governor come amid heightened tensions between the Centre and the PTI-led opposition, with the latter going ahead with its long march despite warnings from the Centre of action against any such move. Hours-long talks over the weekend between a joint delegation of the government and PPP, and the opposition alliance ended in a deadlock , with both sides blaming the other for the breakdown. Political temperatures have also remained high due to speculations of the Centre imposing governor’s rule in the province, with Kundi and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi discussing the move on Sunday. ‘Policy shift is necessary’ The KP CM also reiterated his objection to the Centre’s counterterrorism policy and defended his government’s efforts in supporting the police in the fight against terrorism. He contended that terrorism had been “imposed on the province again”, asserting that the PTI-led provincial government had always supported the police and the people of KP. Afridi maintained that he had been making efforts to strengthen the police, the Counter-Terrorism Department and Special Branch since he took the oath on Oct 15, 2025. “The KP police have the most modern weapons and equipment compared with any other police force in Pakistan,” the chief minister said. He contended that the federal government had always treated KP like a “stepchild”. “The tribal districts were merged into KP in 2018, but they have not been fully integrated financially to this day,” CM Afridi claimed, adding that the financial rights of the tribal districts agreed upon at the time of their merger had not been provided yet. The PTI leader went on to claim that federal governments had “continuously imposed military operations” on KP since 2004. “People displaced by the federal government’s wrong policies kept crying on the streets, but they have still not received full compensation,” he said, adding that nearly Rs100 billion in compensation were still outstanding. “Those whose homes were destroyed, families affected and mosques demolished are still wandering from pillar to post for their compensation.” He highlighted that while a compensation of only Rs400,000 per household had been fixed for tribal families, they had not even been paid the promised amount. Afridi stressed that a commitment was also made to provide between Rs370million and Rs380m per month to displaced people from North Waziristan at the Baka Khel camp . “The displaced people of Baka Khel are still not being provided the monthly amount as promised.” “It is the provincial government’s responsibility to stand with people displaced by the federal government’s wrong policies,” the chief minister stated, adding that his government had provided Rs21bn for displaced people. “The provincial government also has to bear responsibility for losses caused by military operations and collateral damage as a result of drone attacks,” Afridi said. He also remarked that the individuals making decisions in the federal government had no sense of the difficulties faced by the people as a result of those decisions. “If the federal government is sincere with KP, it should upgrade the province’s NFC ( National Finance Commission ) share and pay its outstanding dues of around Rs125bn to the province that has sacrificed 80,000 precious lives,” he demanded. Afridi reaffirmed that KP had to fight terrorism as well as deal with the situation created by the federal government’s policies. “The KP government and police are serious about maintaining law and order. Turning the police into personal servants and assigning them other tasks is wrong,” he declared. “If the policy of KP’s stakeholders is followed, peace can be established within 100 days,” the PTI leader insisted. He questioned why peace could not be established in the province “despite 14,000 intelligence-based operations and 22 major military operations over 22 years”, terming it a “failure of the federal policy”. Afridi maintained that if the issue of peace still exists in KP even after 22 years, the federal government should change its policy against terrorism if it was “serious in doing so”. “The excuse that KP is not cooperating is unacceptable; the same policy is also failing in Balochistan,” he claimed, as both provinces have witnessed an increase in terrorist activities in recent years. “The Balochistan government is cooperating with the federal government, but peace has still not been established there,” Afridi said, claiming the Centre’s counterterrorism policy was neither effective in KP nor in Balochistan. “A shift in policy is necessary. KP can establish peace within 100 days,” he reaffirmed. In his address, Afridi also once again criticised Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s remarks that her province faced no threats from India, despite the state’s narrative of the presence of Indian proxies in Pakistan in the face of Fitna al Hindustan. Asif says ‘enough is enough’ Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif assailed the PTI-led KP government for continuing its “complete detachment from terrorism in the province and criminal indifference”. “Enough is enough!!!” he wrote in a post on X. “The PTI provincial government is roaming the streets for a so-called failed political long march, while its facilitators have unleashed a fresh wave of terrorism against the people of KP during this very time,” he said. The minister recalled Tuesday’s attacks in Dera Ismail Khan , where customs officials were among five people killed. He remarked that the entire provincial cabinet, including the chief minister, was “numb to this serious matter and fully engrossed in their politically failed long march”. “As always, these insensitive and shameless people did not even condemn the innocent murder of these five individuals in DI Khan, offered no condolences to the grieving families, did not attend their funerals or, at the very least, visit their homes to express regret,” Asif regretted. “This is inexcusable by any standard.” Instead, the defence minister noted, the KP CM had scheduled a meeting today at his party’s behest to reprimand the IG and chief secretary for attending the governor’s security meeting. “The chief minister and his cabinet of a province under the scourge of terrorism have completely abandoned the province’s people to the mercy of the terrorists. That is why the people of KP are protesting against the provincial government on the streets in various areas. “This can no longer be tolerated,” Asif declared. The defence minister accused the KP government of being in “complete collusion” with terrorists, saying there was evidence available of “its facilitator ecosystem, which every Pakistani has witnessed with their own eyes over the past three years”. Recalling past arrests of ex-premier Nawaz Sharif and his family members, as well as PML-N leaders, Asif asserted: “Time has proven that the allegations were just allegations and they were imprisoned on Imran Khan’s behest.” Yet, he stressed, the PML-N fulfilled its parliamentary role responsibly under the Constitution and did not hold the country and institutions “hostage”. “It fought a legal and constitutional battle in the courts and parliament. It did not ally with the Taliban,” Asif declared. The defence minister said that the “time has come to make crucial decisions”. “KP cannot be left any longer to the mercy of incompetent, insensitive rulers and Taliban allies,” he avowed. Asif further stressed that the unity of the country cannot be put at risk. “An entire province cannot be held hostage. Enough is enough.”

items.title: Fondements du socialisme aux caractéristiques chinoises: une « Nouvelle ère » de réduction des déséquilibres sociaux et de modernisation
items.description: À l’invitation du Département chargé des communications internationales du Parti communiste chinois (Idcpc), des journalistes et responsables politiques d’une trentaine de pays ont séjourné en Chine du 8 au 16 septembre 2026. Un séjour qui leur a permis de découvrir les fondements du « Socialisme aux caractéristiques chinoises » et ses résultats dans la lutte contre la pauvreté. Le Département chargé des communications internationales du Parti communiste chinois (Idcpc) a organisé, du 8 au 16 septembre 2026, un séminaire en Chine à l’intention des journalistes et des membres de partis communistes d’une trentaine de pays, répartis sur les quatre coins du monde. Une occasion pour les hôtes de s’habituer au socialisme aux caractéristiques chinoises prôné par le président Xi Jinping. C’est un président qui a dédié sa vie au développement de son pays. Le 24 octobre 2017, la pensée du président de la République populaire de Chine, Xi Jinping, a été inscrite dans la charte du Parti communiste chinois (Pcc), au côté de la pensée de Mao Zedong et de la théorie de Deng Xiaoping puis en 2018 dans la Constitution de la République populaire de Chine. Tout comme les responsables du Pcc dans les provinces de Shaanxi et de Zhejiang, Madame Sun Haiyan, vice-ministre chargée de l’Idcpc, est revenue largement sur le socialisme aux caractéristiques chinoises. Une adaptation du marxisme-léninisme aux réalités et aux spécificités de la Chine, se distinguant du modèle capitaliste occidental tout en intégrant certains mécanismes de marché et en s’appuyant sur l’ouverture économique. Sous le président Xi Jinping, explique-t-elle, la Chine est entrée dans une « Nouvelle Ère », marquée par une évolution des priorités. Au-delà de la recherche d’une croissance rapide, l’accent est désormais mis sur un développement plus qualitatif, la réduction des déséquilibres sociaux et la modernisation du pays. « Cette vision est notamment associée au ‘’Rêve chinois’’, qui vise le grand renouveau de la nation chinoise et la construction d’une société socialiste forte et moderne », soutient-elle. Cette politique du président Xi Jinping a permis de sortir plus de 800 millions de personnes de l’extrême pauvreté. La visite au village de Nangou dans la province du Shaanxi a permis de mesurer l’effort fait par la Chine dans la lutte contre la pauvreté. Un village qui se trouve dans le plateau du Lœss, un site marqué à la fois par l’érosion et l’accès à l’eau. Les populations qui ne comptaient que sur l’agriculture et l’élevage voyaient leurs conditions de vie se détériorer. En 1998, des mesures ont été prises pour interdire le pâturage sur certaines collines et restaurer les terres dégradées. Lors d’une visite du Président Xi à Nangou, un village qu’il a visité, à plusieurs reprises, il décida de l’introduction de la culture de pommiers à Nangou, dans la mesure où les conditions géoclimatiques étaient favorables à cette culture. C’est ainsi que des techniciens furent envoyés à Nangou pour encadrer les habitants pour s’approprier cette nouvelle culture. Des retenues d’eau furent créées, et à l’aide de pompes et du système de goutte-à-goutte. Les pommiers s’adaptent. Ils donnent de gros fruits juteux commercialisés maintenant dans les quatre coins du monde. Les populations s’organisent en coopératives et disposent de magasins de stockage. Les conditions de vie changent et le revenu moyen par habitant de ce village de 1.000 âmes monte en flèche, se situant actuellement à 31.000 Rmb, soit 250.000 FCfa. Une prouesse. Le chef de la délégation, le Pdg de la Radiotélévision de Trinidad et Tobago, Michael Kerr, qui a salué les efforts de la Chine dans le cadre de la lutte contre la pauvreté, a mis l’accent sur l’importance des échanges entre le Pcc et l’Idcpc et les partis politiques à travers le monde. Il magnifie les efforts visant à approfondir ces échanges et à renforcer la coopération entre les différentes formations politiques autour de ce qu’il présente comme une cause commune et juste. Pour Michael Kerr, le rapprochement des idées et des intérêts constitue ainsi un élément central dans l’évolution des relations entre partis politiques. Dans son intervention, João Lopes exprime l’intérêt de sa formation politique, le Parti communiste portugais pour l’évolution du socialisme aux caractéristiques chinoises. Il a souligné les réalisations de la Chine sous la direction du Parti communiste chinois et dans le cadre du « socialisme aux caractéristiques chinoises ». Aly DIOUF (de retour de Chine)

items.title: Rent Control urges Parliament to expedite amendment of outdated rent laws
items.description: The Rent Control Department has appealed to Parliament to expedite the amendment of the country’s rent laws, describing the existing legislation as outdated and in need of an overhaul. The department said although it continues to exercise its mandate to regulate relationships between landlords and tenants, including hostel operators, the outdated legal framework poses challenges to effective regulation. The call was made when officials from the Rent Control Department appeared before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC) during its consideration of the 2025 Auditor-General’s Report. A member of the committee and Member of Parliament for Manhyia North, Akwasi Konadu, questioned the department on measures being taken to protect both landlords and tenants, particularly in relation to changes in tenancy arrangements and agreements. In response, Acting Commissioner of the Rent Control Department, Fredrick Opoku, expressed concern about the low level of public education on rent-related laws and regulations. He said the situation was affecting the department’s operations, as many landlords and tenants remained unaware of their rights, responsibilities and the applicable legal provisions. Mr Opoku said the department had therefore intensified efforts to educate the public, particularly property owners and tenants, to improve their understanding of rent laws and enable the department to effectively regulate the sector. He explained that the department had also been cautious in enforcing certain provisions because of the agreements and understandings reached between the parties covered by the law. The Acting Commissioner stressed the need for greater public awareness and an updated legal framework to ensure better protection for both landlords and tenants.

items.title: Emergency, governor's rule would 'definitely' be imposed if deemed necessary to 'save' KP: Kundi
items.description: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said on Wednesday that if the prime minister and the president deemed it necessary to impose an emergency or governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to “save the province” facing terrorism, it would “definitely be enforced”. The governor’s remarks came during Geo News ’ programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath ’, where the possibility of emergency or governor’s rule was discussed. Responding to questions on the subject, Kundi argued that there had been past instances of emergency and governor’s rule being imposed. “In Balochistan, the PPP had to end its government for law and order and impose an emergency,” he remarked. Asked whether an emergency or governor’s rule would be sustainable if imposed, Kundi replied: “The first thing [to decide] is when and whether it is imposed. We can discuss its sustainability in another programme.” This prompted the host to prod Kundi further, saying his remarks indicated that only imposing an emergency or governor’s rule was being considered and its sustainability would addressed later. Kundi said in response, “We have to save the province, we have to establish peace in the province.” The Centre has warned the PTI-led KP government in recent days of sending it packing through an emergency or governor’s rule as the party goes ahead with a protest march to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. Federal ministers have also cited the security situation in KP in this connection, as reiterated by Kundi. Meanwhile, the march remains a major bone of contention between the government and the main opposition party in the Centre, the PTI, with both taking entrenched positions. On Sunday, Interior Mini­ster Mohsin Naqvi also called on Kundi to discuss the political and security situation amid speculations of ‘imminent’ governor’s rule in the province. The meeting was also mentioned in the Geo News programme, with Kundi being asked whether preparations were under way for an emergency or governor’s rule. But Kundi said the PTI’s long march and security-related matters were discussed during the meeting. The KP governor then went on the accuse the provincial government of “facilitating terrorism” and not doing enough to curb it.

items.title: Muere Maricarmen, la mujer que encendió la lucha contra los desahucios en España
items.description: Maricarmen Abascal, la mujer que encendió la lucha contra los desahucios en España, ha fallecido este miércoles en el Hospital Gregorio Marañón a los 87 años, según ha confirmado el Sindicato de Inquilinas en un comunicado. El 23 de septiembre fue desahuciada de su casa de Retiro , en la que vivió durante siete décadas. Seis años antes, una empresa compró su piso por un precio irrisorio para la zona precisamente porque ella vivía en él. Con una pensión de 1.400 euros, la mujer nunca dejó de pagar el alquiler, de renta antigua, y las facturas: unos 500 euros al mes en total. En 2020 los propietarios le dijeron que debía dejar el apartamento, porque el contrato ya había sido subrogado dos veces, primero a su madre ―que no constaba como inquilina, por una ley franquista― y luego a ella. Y desde entonces la intentaron desalojar cuatro veces y no aceptaron ninguna de las propuestas que recibieron para o bien pagar la diferencia del alquiler (le pedían 1.600 euros) o comprar el apartamento. FG can increase workers’ salaries without raising minimum wage — TUC
items.description: —Says govt can pay between N200,000, N400,000 By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — THE Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) on Wednesday, urged the Federal Government to improve workers’ pay immediately, rather than waiting for the next review of the national minimum wage. Briefing journalists in Abuja after its National Administrative Executive Council, NAC meeting, the TUC President, Comrade Festus Osifo, said government could independently increase the salaries of federal workers or raise the pay of the least-paid employees without waiting for a new Minimum Wage Act. He said the minimum wage should be regarded as a statutory wage floor and not a ceiling that prevents government or employers from paying workers substantially above the prescribed minimum. According to him: “Government does not even need to wait for a new Minimum Wage Act to be signed before government will take care of its workers. “Government can wake up today and say, ‘Okay, I want to pay the least-paid worker in the Federal Government payroll N200,000,’ for example. They could say, ‘Let the least-paid worker be N400,000,’ for example, and graduate it upwards. “Is that only the minimum wage for government to do that? No. That is not really the function of a minimum wage.” Osifo argued that employers in several sectors already pay considerably above the statutory minimum, noting that the salaries of university graduates employed by banks, food and beverage companies and oil and gas firms are generally determined by the value of the jobs rather than the national minimum wage. “If you are a university graduate and you are to be employed in a bank, are they going to start you from the minimum wage? The answer is no. The pay you will earn is much above minimum wage,” he said. He added that the same principle applied to major companies in the food and beverage sector. “If you are a university graduate and you are to be employed in the food and beverage industry, if you are to be employed by Nestlé, if you are to be employed by Cadbury, they are not going to look at minimum wage,” he said. The TUC president also cited the oil and gas sector, where he said companies such as Shell, Chevron and TotalEnergies would ordinarily negotiate remuneration based on the nature and value of the jobs rather than the statutory wage floor. “They are going to be talking about living wage,” he said. Osifo therefore urged the Federal Government to take immediate steps to improve workers’ incomes rather than leaving employees to wait for the next statutory minimum wage review. He said TUC had already engaged government officials on the issue, including the Minister of Finance and the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, as part of efforts to push for measures that would improve workers’ welfare. “For us, you don’t really need a new minimum wage to take care of your employees in several sectors. That is not how it is done,” he said. Osifo stressed that allowances could be reviewed independently of the minimum wage, stressing that workers should not be left to bear the full weight of economic reforms until 2027. He said, “Allowances don’t need a minimum wage conversation, and even salaries, government on its own can actually push the salaries of workers up, even without minimum wage conversation.” The current national minimum wage of N70,000 was signed into law in 2024 for a three-year period. Osifo said organised labour was already preparing for the next review, but stressed that government had options for improving workers’ welfare before then. “Government can decide to pay whatever it takes to take care of its employees. Employers can decide to do way above what is there at the minimum threshold,” he said. The post FG can increase workers’ salaries without raising minimum wage — TUC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Traitement de la dette extérieure: le Sénégal rassure ses créanciers
items.description: Après son accord avec le Fonds monétaire international (Fmi), le Sénégal pose un pas de géant dans le cadre du Plan de traitement de la dette. Dans ce cadre, une réunion (en ligne) a été tenue, hier, mardi 6 octobre, avec les créanciers. Les membres de la Direction générale des financements et de la dette (Dgfd) ont rassuré quant aux dispositions du pays à une gestion optimale du portefeuille, avec un calendrier de signature d’accords et d’implémentation. Le Sénégal, à travers la Direction générale des financements et de la dette (Dgfd), a tenu, hier, mardi 6 octobre, une réunion d'information avec des créanciers extérieurs, sous les bons offices du Fonds monétaire international (Fmi). Selon une source, cette entrevue a permis aux autorités de faire le point auprès des créanciers extérieurs sur la situation économique et financière du Sénégal, le programme de réformes économiques et la stratégie de traitement de la dette, y compris le plan d'engagement auprès des créanciers, le calendrier et les prochaines étapes. À côté, les services du Fmi ont présenté les grandes lignes de l'accord conclu au niveau des services avec les autorités concernant un nouvel accord au titre de la Facilité élargie de crédit (Fec), ainsi que les éléments adossés aux politiques et cadres de prêt. Cette rencontre avec les investisseurs entre dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du Plan de traitement de la dette du Sénégal (Ptds). Représenté par Babacar Touré, patron de la Dgfd, et le ministre du Budget, Bassirou Sarr, le Sénégal a souligné qu’il entend poursuivre le traitement de sa dette conformément aux principes du Cadre commun du G20, tout en cherchant à tirer les enseignements et à relever les défis identifiés lors de cas précédents. Les engagements dans ce sens concernent le suivi d’un calendrier accéléré et prévisible pour le traitement de leur créance, sans oublier la clarification rapide des éléments clés qui sous-tendent le Ptds, y compris l’évaluation des contributions. Face aux créanciers extérieurs, le Sénégal a également fixé novembre 2026 comme délai cible pour l’aboutissement des différents cadres du partenariat avec le Fmi. Cela devra se matérialiser par l’approbation du programme par le Conseil d’administration. Dans cette optique, une réunion se tiendra au cours du mois de novembre. En décembre, l’État prévoit de signer des accords de principe avec les Comités des créanciers officiels (Occ) et le groupe ad hoc des détenteurs d’obligations. Ensuite, interviendra, début 2027, la mise en œuvre des accords. Au cours des travaux, le Fmi, selon une source ayant participé à ce rendez-vous, n’a pas beaucoup pris la parole. « Il a laissé le Sénégal présenter sa vision et revenir sur l’évolution de la dette et les mesures correctives », informe-t-elle. Du côté des investisseurs, cet exercice a été bien apprécié. Cependant, certains créanciers bilatéraux ont demandé un traitement sans favoritisme. À la fin des travaux, le Sénégal a rassuré ses partenaires quant à l’organisation périodique de ce type de rencontres. Le stock de la dette extérieure est de 18 300 milliards de FCfa, dont 8500 milliards dus aux banques de développement. La dette commerciale s’élève à 5440 milliards de FCfa et celle bilatérale à 4369 milliards. Demba DIENG

items.title: Police parade suspects over Oyo family-of-six killings
items.description: By Adeola Badru, IBADAN The Oyo State Police Command has paraded several suspects arrested in connection with three separate criminal cases, including the alleged murder of a family of six at Oloba Village in Lagelu Local Government Area of the state. The command said the suspects allegedly attacked the family over a damaged mobile phone belonging to one of them. The other cases involved an alleged armed robbery at Wofun Olodo, Ibadan, during which a 44-year-old woman, Mrs Wahab Rukayat, was reportedly killed, as well as the arrest of a suspected unqualified medical practitioner accused of posing as a doctor. The suspects were paraded at the Police Command Headquarters, Eleyele, Ibadan, where the command provided details of the separate investigations and displayed some of the items allegedly recovered. In the Lagelu case, police identified the three suspects arrested over the alleged murder as Hammed Akinbami, Ojo Akinbami and Padonu Edward. According to the command, the suspects allegedly invaded the residence of Ifeanyi Chukwu, his wife and their four children at Oloba Village, armed with a locally made Dane gun, two cutlasses and a wooden club. Police said the suspects allegedly attacked the family in retaliation for damage to a mobile phone belonging to one of them. The command alleged that the suspects robbed the family of N200,000, a motorcycle, a Doma machine with chainsaw and a spraying machine before using a wooden club to kill four members of the family. It further alleged that the two children who survived the initial attack were taken to the Osun River, where their hands and legs were tied before they were thrown into the river. The police said the remains of the woman had been recovered from the river, while efforts were ongoing to recover the remains of the other members of the family. The command said the suspects were being investigated to establish their individual roles in the alleged attack and the circumstances surrounding the deaths. Three arrested over robbery In a separate case, police paraded three suspected members of an armed robbery gang identified as Oluwatobi Akinrinola, Mathew Okunola and Ibrahim Rabiu. The suspects were arrested over an alleged robbery operation at Wofun Olodo, Ibadan, during which 44-year-old Rukayat was reportedly killed. The command said the suspects allegedly attacked their victims and stole mobile phones, wristwatches, $400 and other valuables estimated at N3.493 million. Police said an iPhone 7 Plus belonging to one of the victims was recovered from the suspects, while surviving victims reportedly identified them during an identification parade. Some of the victims who were invited to the command headquarters to identify the suspects alleged that they were subjected to severe torture during the attacks and that property worth millions of naira was stolen. The police said investigation was ongoing to determine the extent of the suspects’ alleged involvement in the robbery and killing, as well as establish whether other members of the gang were still at large. Suspected fake doctor arrested In the third case, the command paraded Benjamin Adeniyi, described as an auxiliary nurse, for allegedly practising medicine as a doctor without the requisite qualifications and professional training. During an interview, Adeniyi reportedly admitted to the police that he had been practising as a medical doctor since 2022 despite lacking the required qualifications. The police also accused him of operating two hospitals under the name LIFE IS GOOD, with branches in the Olodo and Academy areas of Ibadan, where he allegedly provided medical services, including fertility treatment. The command said investigation was aimed at determining the extent of his activities and identifying patients who may have been exposed to risks as a result of the alleged illegal practice. Reacting to the cases, the Police Public Relations Officer of the command, DSP Olayinka Ayanlade, said investigations into the three incidents were ongoing. Ayanlade said the command was intensifying efforts to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incidents and apprehend other persons who might have been connected with the alleged crimes. He added that the police would continue with the investigations and ensure that anyone found culpable was brought to justice. items.title: No federal project came to South-East before Tinubu — Umahi
items.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA The Minister of Works, Engr. David Umahi, has claimed that the South-East did not benefit from any federal project during his previous political career until the administration of President Bola Tinubu, which he said had deliberately integrated the region into the country’s development agenda. Umahi made the claim at a press briefing in Abuja on Wednesday, where he listed ongoing federal projects in the South-East as evidence of what he described as the Tinubu administration’s commitment to the region. The minister said: “I was party chairman, I was deputy governor, I was governor, and no single federal project came to the South-East. And today, we are having a barrage of projects.” He acknowledged that the South-East might not rank among the regions receiving the highest volume of federal projects but said it was no longer at the bottom. “We may not be first, second or third in terms of volume of projects across regions, but we are not the last. And if we are not the last, it is something to beat our chest about,” Umahi said. He said the development demonstrated what he described as Tinubu’s deliberate effort to integrate the South-East into the affairs of the country. Umahi also described his appointment as Minister of Works as part of the administration’s deliberate approach to the region. “Never in the history of this nation has somebody from the South-East become Minister of Works. This is very intentional, because the President has the intention to develop the South-East, and that is what I am doing,” he said. The minister, who began his remarks by condoling with families of victims of Monday’s Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State, said he believed national unity was linked to what he described as the administration’s policy of inclusion. “This is what we have been waiting for — full integration of the people of the South-East in the affairs of the nation,” he said. According to Umahi, the alleged exclusion of the region in previous administrations had contributed to disunity. “The continuous exclusion of the South-East in the affairs of the nation can never bring unity to this country. So there is unity now. We are happy,” he said. Umahi attacks Obi over economic claims The minister also criticised opposition figures, particularly former Anambra State governor and Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi, accusing them of making promises he considered unsupported and of portraying the South-East negatively. Umahi questioned Obi’s reported claims about savings during his tenure as Anambra governor, describing the argument as poor economics. “What kind of economics allows you to borrow money from financial institutions, spend some and return the rest, and say you are saving?” he asked. He also referred to his participation in meetings of the South-East Governors’ Forum during his tenure as Ebonyi deputy governor, when Obi was governor of Anambra State. “You can’t come out now and deceive our people and say they are just talking. We have had a lot of crises in the South-East, a lot of insecurity, and nobody consoled them,” Umahi said. The minister also defended Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo following criticism over Soludo’s challenge to claims concerning Obi’s debt record while in office. Umahi said Obi should not have expected Soludo to remain silent after what he described as claims about the financial record of the former governor’s administration. “You provoked Soludo. Soludo has not gone into your files. But you cannot say you did not borrow any money and had no debt, and expect the man to shut his mouth,” he said. Umahi urged people of the South-East to continue supporting Tinubu, saying such support could encourage reciprocal political support in the future. “This is the right time. Let us have a handshake across the Niger, so that when our time comes, we will also be supported. Igbo land is not second-class,” he said. items.title: The scars on the drum: A Nunyãdume reflection on failure, courage and the audacity to try
items.description: There is an old lesson in Nunyãdume that the young sometimes understand only after the years have introduced themselves. PART I: Failure is an event and a teacher, not an identity The young person may see a failure as the end of the road because there are not yet enough travelled roads behind him to know how often yesterday’s disappointment becomes tomorrow’s turning point. With the passage of years comes the wisdom of hindsight, the discovery that some doors had to close, some journeys had to fail, and some dreams had to break before we could understand where life was taking us. We begin to see that some of the things we once called failures were lessons; some were redirections; some were warnings; and some were the very wounds through which wisdom entered. The years do not necessarily make us wiser merely because we have grown older. But if we have paid attention, the years give us something youth cannot yet possess in equal measure: the long view, the wisdom of retrospect. The elders therefore say: The drum that has never been beaten may have perfect skin, but it has never summoned a village. Life is much the same. That is why we must be careful what we call failure while the story is still being written. We want the harvest without risking the seed. We want victory without entering the arena. We want the applause without enduring the rehearsal, the criticism, the missed notes and the occasions when the audience does not clap. But that is not how life works. And that is not how greatness is built. Many successful global leaders like Mandela, Nkrumah, and Kofi Annan experienced significant failures. They did not allow failure to define them, but to teach them. In Africa, the farmer understands it. He places seed beneath the earth without a guarantee that every seed will germinate. Some will be eaten by birds. Some will be washed away by rain. Some will encounter poor soil. Some will sprout and die. Yet the farmer returns to the field. Why? Because a failed seed is not a failed farmer. Failure is part of the game Life is a game we enter intending to win. But failure is not necessarily the opposite of winning. Sometimes, failure is part of the price of learning how to win. A child learning to walk does not fall once and conclude, “Walking is not my calling.” He falls. He cries. He rises. He holds the chair. He tries again. And one day, without ceremony, the same feet that repeatedly betrayed him begin carrying him across the room. Nobody calls those early falls failure. We call them development . Why, then, when adults fall while learning to build a business, pursue an education, lead an institution, raise a family, develop an invention or rebuild a life, do we suddenly regard falling as evidence that they were never meant to walk? Failure is often simply knowledge arriving painfully. It tells you: this did not work . It may tell you : not this way . It may tell you : not yet . It may tell you : prepare better . Sometimes it tells you: change direction altogether . But none of those statements means : You are a failure . There is an enormous difference between “I failed at something” and “I am a failure.” One describes an event. The other condemns a human being. And we must never confuse the two. The successful have graves behind them Look carefully at almost every great achievement and you will find a cemetery of abandoned drafts, rejected proposals, wrong turns, embarrassing mistakes and ideas that simply did not work. We sometimes admire successful people only after history has edited out their failures. We see the mansion but not the nights on the floor. We see the degree or certificate but not the examinations failed. We see the company but not the businesses that collapsed before it. We see the leader on the podium but not the elections, applications, appointments, promotions or opportunities lost along the way. We see the harvest. We rarely ask how many planting seasons failed. Yet Nunyãdume knows that the smoothness of the pestle comes from repeated encounters with the mortar . The friction is part of the making . Mistakes are evidence that we are alive There is something deeply human about getting things wrong. We misjudge people. We make poor investments. We trust the wrong advice. We choose badly. We speak when silence would have been wiser and remain silent when courage demanded speech. We sometimes disappoint people we love. And sometimes, after doing everything we knew to do, life still refuses to cooperate. These experiences should produce humility, reflection and growth, not permanent shame. A person who has made no mistakes has attempted very little whose outcome genuinely mattered. The objective, therefore, cannot be never to fail . The objective must therefore be: Never waste a failure . If you fall, collect the lesson before you rise. Otherwise you may have to fall in the same place again. That is the wisdom of Nunyãdume. By

items.title: Insecurity: Nigeria in state of war, TUC laments
items.description: — Says kidnapping still a booming business — Urges FG to double efforts against insecurity By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) on Wednesday lamented that the country has been in a state of war for over a decade due to insecurity, declaring that kidnapping remains a booming business for criminal elements. The union said insecurity has undermined government efforts to attract foreign investment and advised the Federal Government to double its efforts in the fight against insecurity. Briefing journalists after its National Executive Council (NEC) meeting in Abuja, TUC President Comrade Festus Osifo urged the government to strengthen the naira to between ₦700 and ₦800 to one US dollar, saying the high exchange rate remained central to the rising cost of goods, including the petrol pump price. Osifo said the Federal Government should take decisive steps to end the insecurity ravaging the country. He noted that while macroeconomic indicators were improving, with inflation gaining some stability and the exchange rate strengthening, the government could do better. The TUC president recalled that in 2024, the congress presented a 15-point demand to the Federal Government, with the exchange rate at its centre. “We cannot be tired of talking about the exchange rate because it is central to literally everything. Today, the official rate is just a little above ₦1,300 to the USD, but we see that the government can still do better,” he said. “We commend CBN Governor Cardoso for the great work he is doing at the Central Bank, but we can still do much more because we still believe that ₦1,300 to $1 is still undervalued.” Comrade Osifo stressed that the naira should trade between ₦700 and ₦800 to $1, insisting that at ₦1,300 it remains undervalued. “From all international commentators, from economic think tanks, both local and international, and from scholars, currently our naira is undervalued and is not trading at the strength it should. “Yes, we knew that before, when it was around ₦400, it was overvalued, but today at ₦1,300 it is still undervalued. So the government should do everything possible to move the naira to the right value,” Osifo said. He also commiserated with the families of security personnel who died in recent incidents, noting that one of the pilots involved had gotten married just weeks earlier. On insecurity, Osifo said the TUC wanted the Federal Government to deal decisively with the problem ravaging almost every part of the country. He said the union was urging the government to provide security agencies with the needed funds and equipment to prosecute the fight against terrorists and bandits, adding that without a stable country there would be no economic progress. He condemned the incident in Niger State that led to the death of about 37 persons in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), describing it as an aberration. “We are quite happy that the government immediately swung into action by setting up a committee, but we don’t want the committee’s report to just be another report gathering dust. Whoever is culpable, no matter how highly placed, must be decisively dealt with according to the letter and spirit of the law,” he said. Addressing the country’s many security challenges, the TUC president said: “First, as you know, gentlemen of the press, today we have been facing the issue of insecurity in our country, maybe in the last 15 years at best. “And in our last press briefing, we extended a thank you to the DG of the DSS for the great work he has been doing, seeing the number of convictions in recent times, with a number of apprehensions without paying ransom. We still commend him on that. “And we still wish that they continue on that trajectory. Same with the National Security Adviser; we know that they don’t sleep on a daily basis in order to make the rest of us sleep. “Having said that, we know, as a country, that we are still faced with a huge level of insecurity. For example, recently, as we all know, the level of kidnapping and killings in the Bakin Ladi area in Plateau State has even increased much more. “We know very well, for a fact, that in some areas in our country—states like Zamfara, Borno, Katsina, even in the southern part of the country, and Nigeria in general—we have kidnappings still going on as a business. “We have killings still going on. We have proposed at a time, as the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, that the government should even carry out what we call virement in the budget to move funds to that area to procure the necessary equipment, to procure all the necessary gadgets to wipe out these people once and for all, because Nigeria has been in a state of war for over a decade, and we must stamp this out once and for all. “It is very difficult to attract foreign investment. It’s very difficult to even get local investors to put their money into the economy where there is this level of uncertainty and this level of insecurity. “So for us, the government should double its effort. The funds going to fight the state of insecurity should be increased. Yes, we love road construction. Yes, we love investment in power. We love investment in education and so on and so forth. But beyond that, we must first of all live well. We must first of all be alive to enjoy the dividends of the infrastructures—to be able to drive on those roads, to be able to feed and to send our children to school. “So the protection of life and property should be paramount to any government. Yes, we could see that a lot is being done, but we are encouraging them to do much more.” On the health sector dispute involving members of the Joint Health Sector Unions (JOHESU), Osifo said the union had resolved to send a letter to the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare to hasten action on the workers’ demands. The post Insecurity: Nigeria in state of war, TUC laments appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: N70,000 minimum wage fails decent living — Labour
items.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young & Omotola Aremo LAGOS The Association of Senior Staff of Banks, Insurance and Financial Institutions, ASSBIFI, on Wednesday said the N70,000 national minimum wage was inadequate to guarantee decent living for Nigerian workers. The union described the wage as grossly insufficient to meet workers’ basic needs, saying it “does not take the worker to the bus stop.” ASSBIFI made the declaration in Lagos during its commemoration of the 2026 World Day for Decent Work, where it called on the Federal Government to take urgent steps to reduce the rising cost of living and improve workers’ welfare. Acting National President of ASSBIFI, Fanimokun Adesina, said workers deserved wages capable of supporting their families and ensuring a dignified standard of living. “We demand an end to indecent work. The worker deserves living wages, not the N70,000 stipend that does not take the worker to the bus stop. “We demand wages that enhance living standards and social protection that guarantees dignity and after-work survival,” he said. Adesina described as “absurd” a situation where the national minimum wage could neither purchase a bag of rice nor pay the monthly rent of an average family. He said: “A situation whereby the national minimum wage cannot buy a bag of rice is absurd; a situation whereby the national minimum wage cannot pay monthly house rent for an average family of six is absurd. “A situation where the national minimum wage cannot provide three square meals for an average Nigerian family of four for two weeks is nothing but slavery. “Workers are not slaves; we must be treated with the dignity that decent work reflects.” He called on the Federal Government to urgently implement policies to reduce the pressure on workers, particularly by addressing the cost of food, transportation, healthcare, housing and education, while also improving national security. FG moves to review labour laws Meanwhile, the Zonal Director, Southwest and State Controller, Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment, Mrs Mienye Badejo, said the ministry was pushing for a review of relevant labour laws to reflect changing workplace practices. Badejo disclosed this in a goodwill message at the ASSBIFI event, where she noted that technological changes and evolving employment practices were reshaping the workplace, particularly in the banking and insurance sectors. Represented by a ministry official, Mrs Franca Shaabu, Badejo said the ministry would continue to engage critical stakeholders and push for the review of existing labour laws to make them compatible with emerging hybrid and flexible working arrangements. “The ministry will continue to liaise with all critical stakeholders and push for the review of relevant extant labour laws to make them more compatible with emerging hybrid and flexible working arrangements,” she said. items.title: Espagne : Pedro Rodríguez raccroche les crampons à 39 ans
items.description: L’attaquant espagnol Pedro Rodríguez, ancien joueur phare du FC Barcelone et de la sélection espagnole, a officialisé mercredi sa retraite du football professionnel à l’âge de 39 ans. L’annonce a été faite à travers une vidéo publiée sur ses réseaux sociaux et tournée au Camp Nou, l’enceinte mythique où le natif de Tenerife a lancé sa carrière et s’est imposé comme l’un des piliers de l’ère dorée de Pep Guardiola. « Je sens que c’est le moment d’achever une étape merveilleuse », a confié « Pedrito », en revenant sur les moments forts d’un parcours exceptionnel. Formé au Barça, Pedro y a remporté l’ensemble des grands trophées possibles, contribuant à faire de cette équipe l’une des plus titrées de l’histoire du football. Son palmarès sous le maillot blaugrana comprend notamment cinq Ligas, trois Ligues des champions, trois Coupes du Roi, quatre Supercoupes d’Espagne, trois Supercoupes d’Europe et deux Coupes du monde des clubs. En 2009, l’attaquant est entré dans l’histoire en devenant le premier joueur à inscrire au moins un but dans six compétitions de clubs différentes au cours d’une même saison : Liga, Coupe du Roi, Ligue des champions, Supercoupe d’Espagne, Supercoupe d’Europe et Coupe du monde des clubs. Sur le plan international, il a été un élément clé de la « Roja », sacrée championne du monde en Afrique du Sud en 2010, puis championne d’Europe en 2012. Après son départ de Catalogne en 2015, l’international espagnol a poursuivi sa carrière en Angleterre sous les couleurs de Chelsea, avant de rejoindre l’Italie, où il a évolué à l’AS Roma puis à la Lazio, son dernier club. The post Espagne : Pedro Rodríguez raccroche les crampons à 39 ans appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Army takes over Old Oyo Park as training ground
items.description: By Adeola Badru The Nigerian Army has taken over the entire stretch of the Old Oyo National Park in Oyo State as a training ground in a move aimed at preventing a recurrence of the abduction of pupils, children and teachers in Oriire Local Government Area of the state. The General Officer Commanding, GOC, 2 Division, Nigerian Army, Major-General Auwalu Mahmuda, disclosed this on Wednesday when he received members of the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigerian Union of Journalists, NUJ, Oyo State Council, at the division’s headquarters in Odogbo, Ibadan. Mahmuda said the decision followed the abduction and subsequent rescue of the Oriire victims, explaining that the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant-General Waidi Shuaibu, had directed the 2 Division to use the Old Oyo National Park as a military training site. He said the move would make it more difficult for kidnappers and other criminals to use the vast forest as a hideout or base for criminal activities. “On the order of the Chief of Army Staff, Lt. General Waidi Shuaibu, the 2 Division has taken over the entire stretch of the Old Oyo National Park as a training site in order to prevent the repeat of the Oriire kidnap saga. “With the 2 Division fully utilising the park, it will be a herculean task for men of the underworld to use it as their hideout,” he said. The GOC also stressed the need for stronger collaboration between the military and the media, particularly in tackling misinformation and fake news, which he said could cause serious damage when information was published or broadcast without proper verification. He urged journalists to verify information obtained from their sources with the military before making it available to the public, warning that unverified reports could cause “irreparable damage” and worsen the situation they were intended to address. “I will appeal to you to avoid publishing information without first confirming its exact and true nature with the military. Sometimes, when unverified information is released, it can cause more harm than the information it intended to address,” he said. Mahmuda said misinformation could spread rapidly and cause serious consequences, urging journalists to exercise caution in reporting security-related matters. He said the media had a critical role to play in supporting national development and keeping the public properly informed about the efforts of security agencies to combat insecurity. “I want to reassure you that the Nigerian Army sees journalists as partners, but they are also expected to play their part in demonstrating clearly that they are partners of the Nigerian Army,” he said. The GOC commended members of the Correspondents’ Chapel for consistently reporting the activities and contributions of the 2 Division to national development. He said the military and the media, despite operating in different environments, remained Nigerians working towards the same national objective. “We are all Nigerians, irrespective of the fact that some of us wear uniforms. I believe that, whatever we are doing, we are all working towards the success and development of this country,” Mahmuda said. He appealed for closer collaboration among the Army, the media and other security agencies in educating the public on ongoing efforts to tackle insecurity across the country. According to him, journalists often put their lives at risk while gathering and reporting information, particularly when covering dangerous areas. “I have seen journalists go to places where other civilians dare not set their foot. They put themselves in difficult and dangerous situations simply to obtain accurate information that can be shared with the public,” he said. Mahmuda also reassured journalists of the Nigerian Army’s continued support, promising assistance to the Oyo State Correspondents’ Chapel in areas including training and medical outreach, particularly as the chapel prepares for its forthcoming Press Week. Earlier, the Chairman of the Correspondents’ Chapel, Mr Yinka Adeniran, commended the 2 Division for its sustained efforts towards maintaining security in the state and beyond. Adeniran specifically praised the division for its role in the successful rescue of victims of the Oriire abduction, describing the operation as a demonstration of the security forces’ commitment to protecting lives and property. He also appealed to the division to support the chapel’s forthcoming Press Week, particularly in the areas of a lecture and medical outreach for members, among other activities. items.title: Gender Ministry warns perpetrators of violence after Nana Akua Addo videos circulate
items.description: The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection has warned that persons who perpetrate violence against women and children will be held accountable under the law. The warning follows the widespread circulation of videos and images on social media reportedly involving actress and fashion personality Nana Akua Addo and her child. Some of the footage appears to show Ms Addo with visible injuries following a physical altercation, while separate footage purportedly shows a child being subjected to physical violence. The Ministry, however, stressed that the full facts and circumstances surrounding the reported incidents were still being established. In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 6, the Ministry said it was deeply concerned about the images and reports and reiterated that violence in all its forms must not be normalised, excused or tolerated. “The Ministry takes this opportunity to send a strong and unequivocal message to all persons who perpetrate violence against women, children or any other person. Such acts have no place in our society. Persons who subject others to violence and abuse will be held accountable in accordance with the law,” it said. The Ministry noted that the Domestic Violence Act, 2007 (Act 732), provides a legal framework for the protection of persons from domestic violence, while the Children’s Act, 1998 (Act 560), provides for the protection and welfare of children. It said it was closely following developments and taking steps, together with the appropriate institutions, to ascertain the wellbeing and safety of the persons involved and determine the necessary interventions. The Ministry stressed that no relationship, domestic circumstance, disagreement or perceived provocation could justify violence or abuse. It also urged women and other persons experiencing domestic, gender-based or other forms of violence not to suffer in silence or accept abuse as a normal part of any relationship. “Abuse is never the fault of the victim and silence only emboldens perpetrators,” the Ministry said. It encouraged victims and anyone with credible information about a person at risk to report incidents to the nearest police station or Social Welfare office. The Ministry also appealed to the public to refrain from sharing the graphic videos, personal information and unverified claims concerning Ms Addo and her child. It said although the public concern surrounding the reports was understandable, continued circulation of the material could further expose and distress those involved, particularly the child. The appeal comes after Ms Addo’s legal representatives also asked media organisations and the public to stop publishing or sharing the videos, particularly footage involving a minor. Her lawyers said the matter was before the appropriate authorities and urged the media to respect the privacy of the family. The Ministry said it remained committed to protecting the dignity, safety and wellbeing of women and children and would continue working with relevant institutions to ensure that persons affected by violence received the necessary protection, care and support. items.title: Gouvernement : le RNI refuse de faire pression pour participer, tout en laissant la porte ouverte
items.description: Alors que les consultations pour la formation du prochain gouvernement se poursuivent, le Rassemblement national des indépendants (RNI) adopte une position prudente. Le parti ne compte ni réclamer une place au gouvernement ni anticiper un éventuel passage dans l’opposition, préférant laisser les consultations déterminer la configuration de la prochaine majorité. Le débat existe pourtant bel et bien au sein du parti. Selon une source dirigeante, certaines voix se sont prononcées en faveur d’un passage dans l’opposition depuis l’annonce des résultats des élections législatives. Cette orientation aurait notamment été exprimée lors de la réunion du Conseil national du RNI tenue samedi à Rabat. Pour ces membres du parti, l’opposition pourrait constituer une option politique cohérente au regard des résultats du scrutin et de la nouvelle configuration du paysage politique et parlementaire. Cette tendance ne constitue toutefois pas la position officielle du RNI. Le Conseil national a déjà exprimé la disponibilité du parti à participer au prochain gouvernement et a confié à son président, Mohamed Chouki, le soin de gérer cette participation conformément à ce qu’il considère comme l’intérêt national. Le parti n’a cependant pas formulé, jusqu’à présent, de demande officielle en faveur d’une participation au gouvernement. Il n’a pas non plus décidé de rejoindre l’opposition. Cette ligne permet au RNI de conserver les deux options ouvertes alors que les consultations conduites par Fatima-Zahra El Mansouri, chargée de former le prochain gouvernement, se poursuivent. « L’important, c’est que le tort ne vienne pas de nous » C’est dans cette logique qu’un responsable du RNI résume la position actuelle du parti : « l’important à cette étape est que le tort ne vienne pas de nous ». À travers cette formule, le parti entend surtout ne pas apparaître comme la formation qui chercherait à imposer sa présence dans le prochain exécutif. Le RNI ne souhaite donc pas faire pression pour obtenir une participation, ni devancer le résultat des consultations en annonçant un passage dans l’opposition. Il entend se déterminer à partir de la configuration qui émergera du dialogue entre les différentes formations politiques. Le PAM garde la main Cette posture place également le Parti Authenticité et Modernité (PAM), arrivé en tête des dernières élections législatives, au centre du processus de construction de la majorité. Selon la source citée par Hespress , la responsabilité de définir les contours de la prochaine coalition revient d’abord au parti arrivé en tête et à Fatima-Zahra El Mansouri, qui conduit les consultations. Le RNI affirme ainsi ne pas vouloir se placer en position de force dans les négociations, ni imposer ses propres conditions pour intégrer le prochain gouvernement. Cette approche contraste avec une éventuelle logique de négociation fondée sur les portefeuilles ministériels ou les postes à pourvoir : pour l’instant, le sujet n’est pas présenté comme une priorité par la formation. Le débat sur la participation reste ouvert Le fait que le RNI ne fasse pas pression pour participer ne signifie pas pour autant que l’option gouvernementale est abandonnée. Le parti de la Colombe demeure ouvert à une intégration dans la prochaine majorité, conformément à la position arrêtée par son Conseil national. Mais cette disponibilité reste conditionnée à l’évolution des consultations et à la configuration finale de la coalition. À l’intérieur du parti, le débat entre participation et opposition devrait donc se poursuivre, notamment en fonction des équilibres qui se dessinent autour du PAM. Pas encore de noms pour le gouvernement La question des futurs ministres circule déjà dans les discussions politiques, mais aucune liste officielle n’existe encore du côté du RNI. La source citée par Hespress dément notamment qu’un membre de la famille de Mohamed Chouki ou qu’une autre personnalité précise ait été officiellement retenue pour entrer au gouvernement. À ce stade, le parti considère que l’ordre des priorités est différent : d’abord déterminer s’il participera, ensuite discuter des conditions de cette participation et, enfin, des profils susceptibles d’être proposés. Cette prudence intervient après des élections qui ont modifié les rapports de force au sein de la Chambre des représentants. Le RNI, qui dirigeait le gouvernement au cours de la précédente législature, doit désormais composer avec une nouvelle configuration politique dans laquelle le PAM occupe la première place. Le choix entre majorité et opposition représente donc une décision importante pour le parti, après cinq années passées aux responsabilités. Le débat interne ne porte pas uniquement sur la présence au gouvernement. Il concerne également le rôle que le RNI souhaite jouer dans la nouvelle séquence politique et parlementaire. Toutefois, la question de la participation ne concerne pas seulement le RNI. Le Parti de l’Istiqlal s’est déjà orienté vers une participation au prochain gouvernement. L’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP) semble également se rapprocher de cette option, même si son Conseil national doit encore se prononcer définitivement, alors que le Parti du progrès et du socialisme (PPS) poursuit, de son côté, sa réflexion sur son propre positionnement. Dans ce contexte, la construction de la prochaine majorité pourrait prendre une forme différente de celle de la législature précédente, avec la possibilité d’une présence plus importante des formations issues de la « Koutla ». The post Gouvernement : le RNI refuse de faire pression pour participer, tout en laissant la porte ouverte appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Man City should ‘accept’ punishment for rule breaches, says Lineker
items.description: Gary Lineker has called on Manchester City to “accept whatever punishment” they are given for the good of the game after the club were found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules. An independent commission said last week that City had arranged “sham” contracts with a number of their commercial partners to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs over a nine-season period, between 2009 and 2018. The 10-time English champions, who continue to deny any wrongdoing, confirmed on Friday that they had appealed against the judgement. No sanction has yet been decided upon but City could face substantial points deductions, a fine or even expulsion from the Premier League. “Obviously, it looks really bad for Manchester City, and bad for the game, too,” former England captain Lineker said on Wednesday at Leaders Week London 2026, held at Chelsea’s Stamford Bridge stadium. “When they talk about the ‘Premier League conspiracy theories’, you just think to yourself, ‘Well, this is actually the last thing in the world that the Premier League would want’. “So, I’d love to see Man City now just own it and just say, ‘OK, we got it wrong but for the good of the game, we’ll accept it and we’ll accept whatever punishment comes our way and we’ll carry on’. “That would be a blessing and save their face a little bit at the moment, although it doesn’t look likely.” Pressed as to whether City should be stripped of the three league titles they won during the period in question, 65-year-old Lineker said: “I wouldn’t be surprised if it goes down that route. But who suffers from that? The players and the fans.” Kyle Walker, who spent eight years at City, winning multiple trophies before his departure in 2025, said that the players would always have the memories of their achievements, “whatever happens”. The Burnley right-back, speaking on Talksport, said: “It’s something that we probably don’t want to talk about because we want to be looked upon as winning (those) trophies and winning them the right way. “It’s very difficult because we’ve worked very hard for them, and not just us. I look at the fans that have travelled up and down the country, travelled abroad to Istanbul when we won the treble, and they deserve that night as well.” The post Man City should ‘accept’ punishment for rule breaches, says Lineker appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Parents jubilate as abducted 20 NYSC prospective corps members regain freedom
items.description: By Adeola Badru Parents of the 20 prospective members of the National Youth Service Corps, NYSC, who were abducted while travelling to their orientation camps in Imo State, have expressed relief and joy following confirmation of their release. The parents, however, said their joy was mixed with anxiety as they were yet to establish direct contact with their children amid reports that the released prospective corps members were still with the Department of State Services, DSS. One of the affected parents and spokesperson for the families, Alhaja Alimot Akande, confirmed the release in an interview with Vanguard on Wednesday, saying the development had brought considerable relief to families who had spent days in anguish over the fate of their children. Akande, who has been at the forefront of efforts by the affected families to secure the release of the prospective corps members, said the parents were grateful that their children had regained their freedom but stressed that the ordeal had taken a heavy emotional and financial toll on the families. She said: “We are happy that they have been released. This is what every parent has been waiting and praying for. For days, we have been living in fear and uncertainty because we did not know what could happen to our children. “Now that we have heard that they have been released, we thank God for preserving their lives. But our joy is not yet complete because we have not been able to speak with them ourselves. “What we have heard is that they are still with the DSS. So, we are waiting for the authorities to allow us to have contact with them and, most importantly, to reunite them with their families.” Akande said the release had also imposed a financial burden on the affected families, explaining that individual parents had made separate arrangements following ransom demands allegedly communicated by the abductors. “The individual parents were responsible for the release in their separate ways because the abductors had given their words on the amount of ransom involved. “Each family had to find a way of dealing with its own situation. We were all desperate to see our children come back alive, and that was the priority for every parent,” she said. She also said no government had provided the affected families with financial assistance towards securing the release of their children. “No government gave us anything to support the families towards the release of our children. We had to do what we could as individual families. “Everybody was looking for a way to bring their child back safely. It was not an easy thing for any of us, but we were prepared to do whatever was necessary within our means to ensure that our children returned alive,” she said. According to Akande, the families endured sleepless nights and emotional distress throughout the period of the abduction because they were uncertain about the condition of their children. “The psychological trauma has been enormous. Imagine having your child travelling to report for NYSC and then you suddenly hear that the vehicle they were travelling in had been attacked and the occupants abducted. “You cannot sleep properly. You cannot eat properly. You are constantly thinking about where your child is, what the child is going through and whether the child is still alive,” she said. She appealed to the authorities to ensure that the released prospective corps members received proper care before being reunited with their families. “Now that they have been released, our appeal is that the government and security agencies should ensure that these children are properly attended to. “They need medical attention, psychological support and every necessary assistance because they have gone through a traumatic experience. They should not simply be released and left to deal with the experience on their own,” Akande said. She also called for stronger security arrangements for prospective corps members travelling to orientation camps, saying the incident had exposed the vulnerability of young Nigerians fulfilling their national service obligations. “These are young Nigerians who were simply going to serve their country. They should not be exposed to this kind of danger while travelling to their orientation camps. “We hope that the authorities will learn from what has happened and put measures in place to prevent a recurrence. The safety of prospective corps members should be taken seriously,” she said. One of the affected parents, Mr Femi Adewale, 53, a public servant and father of Feyisayo, one of the abducted prospective corps members, also expressed relief over the development. Adewale said: “We are very happy and relieved that our children have been released. It has been a very difficult period for us as parents because we did not know what would happen to them. “The most important thing for us now is to see our children, speak with them and know that they are safe. We thank God for preserving their lives.” Similarly, Mrs Sade Oyeyemi, 51, whose only daughter, Kemisola, was among those abducted, said the confirmation of the release had brought immense relief to her family after days of anxiety. Oyeyemi said: “I am very happy that she has been released. As a mother, especially when the child involved is your only daughter, you cannot explain the kind of fear and pain you go through when you do not know where she is or what is happening to her. “We have been praying and hoping that they would be released alive. Now that we have heard that they have been released, we are grateful to God. We only want to see her, hear her voice and know that she is truly safe.” Another affected parent, 55-year-old Janet Oladosu, also expressed gratitude over the development, saying the confirmation had brought relief after days of fear and sleepless nights. Oladosu said: “The news of their release is a great relief to us. We have been living in fear and praying for our children. Nobody wants to hear that their child has been abducted, especially when the child was simply travelling to begin the National Youth Service. “We thank God that they are alive and have been released. What we need now is for them to be brought back safely to their families.” The development followed confirmation by the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, who received the news from Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodinma, during a telephone conversation at about 5pm on Wednesday. According to a statement by the Olubadan’s media aide, Adeola Oloko, Uzodinma personally conveyed confirmation of the release to the monarch. The development has brought relief to the families and relatives of the prospective corps members, who had remained anxious since their abduction while travelling towards their orientation camps in Imo State. The Olubadan, who had closely monitored developments concerning the abducted prospective corps members, also expressed relief following confirmation of their release. However, the affected families said their immediate priority remained the safe return of their children and direct confirmation of their physical and emotional condition after the ordeal. They also appealed to the relevant authorities to provide the released prospective corps members with appropriate medical and psychological support, stressing that the experience could have lasting emotional consequences. The post Parents jubilate as abducted 20 NYSC prospective corps members regain freedom appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Accra prépare sa candidature pour rejoindre les BRICS
items.description: Le Ghana veut franchir une nouvelle étape dans la diversification de ses partenariats internationaux. Le Conseil des ministres a donné son feu vert de principe à une candidature officielle du pays aux BRICS, a annoncé, le mardi 6 octobre 2026, le ministre des Affaires étrangères, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa. Accra a déjà sollicité l’appui de l’Inde. Le Ghana pourrait bientôt rejoindre les rangs des pays souhaitant intégrer les BRICS. Le Conseil des ministres a approuvé le principe d’une candidature officielle du pays à ce groupe de puissances émergentes, a indiqué le chef de la diplomatie ghanéenne. «Le Conseil des ministres du président John Dramani Mahama a décidé que le Ghana devait déposer une candidature officielle pour rejoindre les BRICS», a déclaré Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, lors d’une conférence de presse tenue avec son homologue indien, Subrahmanyam Jaishankar. Dans le cadre de cette démarche, Accra a déjà approché New Delhi afin d’obtenir son soutien. Pour les autorités ghanéennes, une éventuelle adhésion aux BRICS s’inscrit dans une volonté de multiplier les partenariats économiques et diplomatiques du pays, notamment avec les nations du Sud global. Créé en 2009 par le Brésil, la Russie, l’Inde et la Chine, le groupe s’est progressivement élargi. L’Afrique du Sud l’a rejoint en 2010. En 2024, l’Égypte, l’Éthiopie, l’Iran et les Émirats arabes unis ont intégré le bloc, avant l’adhésion de l’Indonésie en 2025. Pour Accra, intégrer cette plateforme pourrait notamment contribuer à élargir ses débouchés commerciaux, diversifier ses partenaires économiques et renforcer sa coopération avec les pays membres. Un soutien indien, mais une décision collective Selon plusieurs sources, l’Inde a accueilli favorablement la démarche du Ghana. New Delhi a toutefois rappelé que l’entrée d’un nouveau membre dans les BRICS reste soumise à l’examen et à l’approbation de l’ensemble des pays membres. La candidature ghanéenne devra donc encore franchir cette étape collective avant qu’Accra puisse éventuellement faire son entrée dans le groupe. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Accra prépare sa candidature pour rejoindre les BRICS est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .
